title: chore(website): upgrade to React 19 and Tailwind 4
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Step 1 of moving pollinations.ai to the v2 site (#14472) one piece at a time. Same pages, new stack, no visible change.

- React 18 → 19; `react-dom/client` added to the `vendor` chunk so app code stays in its own chunk.
- Tailwind 3 → 4 via `@tailwindcss/vite`; removes `postcss.config.js` and `autoprefixer`. `tailwind.config.ts` is still loaded through `@config`.
- Classes rewritten by `@tailwindcss/upgrade` (for example `flex-shrink-0` → `shrink-0`, `!` moved to the end).
- Restores two v3 defaults that v4 changed: gray-200 default border colour and the pointer cursor on buttons. Adds `md:leading-none` to page titles, where v3's `md:text-5xl` line height had overridden `leading-tight`.

**Verification** (old and new builds side by side, same recorded API responses, 1440px and 390px):
- `/`, `/apps`, `/community`, `/terms`, `/privacy`, `/refunds`: every element has the same position, size, colours, borders and shadows.
- `/play`: only the 9px 💎 on paid models differs. Its line box shrinks from 24px to 13.5px because v4 line heights are unitless, so the glyph moves by under 1px.
- `npm run build` (tsc + vite) and `npm test` pass.
- Bundle: vendor JS is 53.9 → 77.4 kB gzip (React 19); CSS is 8.5 → 9.9 kB gzip.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

gist.headline: New engine, same garden
gist.blurb: The website gets React 19 and Tailwind 4 under the hood. The flowers stay exactly where they were.
gist.summary: The website moves from React 18 to 19 and Tailwind 3 to 4, retaining its existing pages and matching layouts while laying groundwork for the v2 site.
gist.impact: Visitors keep the same page layouts and styling; the upgrade preserves Tailwind 3’s default border colour and button cursor behavior.
gist.visual_concept: Show the existing pollinations.ai garden storefront unchanged while Polli, wearing a tiny tool belt, and the monitor robot gently replace its hidden machinery. Matching flowers and windows make the behind-the-scenes nature of the upgrade clear.

Cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, with a soft lime green (#ecf874) and pastel gradient background, chunky retro sprites, and a nostalgic, emotionally warm feel like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike.
